title: Homemade Apple Cider
description: Apples, orange and spices slow-cooked, mashed and strained.

ingredients.item: Apples, a sweet and tart mix (about half Honeycrisp, half Granny Smith)

steps.do: Peel the orange and put only the segments into a 4-quart or larger slow cooker; peel and pith make the cider bitter. Quarter the apples, cut out the cores and add them, then the cinnamon, cloves and sugar.
uses: Apples, a sweet and tart mix (about half Honeycrisp, half Granny Smith)

steps.do: Pour in water until the fruit is just covered. Any more dilutes the flavor.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours (the better option) or on high for 4 hours, until the fruit is very soft.
steps.wait: 6 to 7 hr on low, or 4 hr on high

steps.do: Fish out the cinnamon sticks, mash the fruit thoroughly with a potato masher or sturdy spoon, then return the sticks and cover.
Cook 1 hour more on either setting.
Strain slowly through a fine-mesh sieve into a pot or heatproof pitcher, then strain a second time to catch the remaining solids. Serve warm.

notes: Apples: mix sweet (Jazz, Honeycrisp, Sugarbee, Pink Lady, Gala, Fuji, Cortland) with tart (Granny Smith, Braeburn, Jonathan, Pacific Rose). An all-tart batch comes out thin on sweetness and less balanced.
Sugar: 1/4 cup (50 g) for a spicier cider, 1/2 cup (100 g) for store-bought sweetness. Brown sugar swaps in at the same amount. Honey works too; stir it in at the end until it tastes right.
Whole cloves taste the same as ground but give a noticeably paler cider.

Stovetop: combine everything in a large stockpot and bring to a simmer over high heat, stirring now and then. Cover, drop to medium-low and simmer 2 hours, then mash, re-cover and simmer 1 hour more. Leave headroom; a 5-quart Dutch oven can boil over under the lid.
Storage: refrigerate up to 5 to 7 days and rewarm on the stove, or drink it cold. Freezes up to 3 months; ice cube trays make single servings. Thaw in the fridge.
Leftover mash: use it like spiced applesauce in apple cake or muffins, trimming that recipe's sugar a little. Simmer it to thicken if it's watery.
